01 / WIRE YOUR SENSOR

A simple connection.

For an ESP32 development board with USB and a short sensor cable.

Device offlineWaiting for a live reading
ESP32WROOM-32D
3V3VCC
GPIO 27DATA
GNDGND
DHT22AM2302

Use a 4.7k–10kΩ pull-up between DATA and 3V3 if your sensor does not already have one. Identify pins from your sensor's markings; wire colours vary. Keep the cable under 1 m.

02 / FIND YOUR SERVER

Keep it on the same Wi-Fi.

Use a 2.4 GHz network for the ESP32. The PC can use Ethernet or Wi-Fi on the same LAN.

Your PC needs to stay on while collecting measurements. Allow Node.js through Windows Firewall on your private network if prompted.

03 / FLASH WITH ARDUINO IDE

Your sensor, ready to go.

Install esp32 by Espressif Systems, DHT sensor library by Adafruit, and Adafruit Unified Sensor.

The download includes your server address and device token when opened from localhost. Only your Wi-Fi credentials need editing. If your PC has multiple network adapters, verify the selected address. This prototype uses local HTTP and is intended for your trusted LAN.
